submission.natural_language_explanation: This layer-0 pole is a token-identity detector for the Greco-Roman classical and Greco-Latin learned lexicon: it fires on the token currently being read when that token is ' Greek'/'Greece', a Greek-alphabet letter, a classical Greek or Roman name or antiquity (Achilles, Odysseus, Plato, Caesar, legion, gladiator, Rome, Carthage), or a Latin/Greek word-part inside such vocabulary ('us' as in vagus/nucleus/mucus, 'itus' as in emeritus/mellitus, and 'orth-', 'cran-', 'path-', '-onic', '-acter', 'parap-'). It stays at or below baseline on ordinary English words that merely contain the same letter strings (bus, bonus, status, north, iconic, character), on modern Latinate vocabulary (history, democracy, biology, school) and on non-classical ancient cultures (Hindu, Buddhist, Sanskrit, Egyptian), so the trigger is the token's Greco-Latin classical identity rather than its spelling or the surrounding context.

The recurrent laryngeal nerve (RLN) is a branch of the vagus nerve (cranial nerve X) that supplies all the intrinsic muscles of the larynx, with the exception of the cricothyroid muscles. There are two recurrent laryngeal nerves, right and left, in the human body. adversarial_test_results.detail: Modern Latinate vocabulary (history, democracy, biology, school) that the hypothesis says stays at or below baseline.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Hindu temples, Buddhist stupas, Sanskrit texts and Egyptian tombs fill the museum.

adversarial_test_results.detail: parapet contains the parap- spelling but is an Italian loanword, not the Greek word-part the hypothesis triggers on.
